key_insight: The paper argues that machine learning in high-energy nuclear physics is shifting from isolated pattern recognition toward physics-integrated pipelines that directly infer properties of QCD matter and related systems under physical constraints.
engineering_relevance: This matters for computational science because it shows how ML can accelerate inverse problems, surrogate modeling, and uncertainty-aware parameter extraction in complex multi-physics workflows.
method: Bayesian calibration and inverse inference for QCD matter and dense-matter equation of state
Physics-aware generative modeling, neural unfolding, and differentiable solvers for weak signals and inverse problems
Symmetry- and constraint-preserving models such as gauge-equivariant samplers and diffusion-based lattice-field methods
evidence_signal: The abstract is a mini-review of recent work across heavy-ion collisions, neutron-star physics, lattice QFT, and holographic or continuum QCD, emphasizing validation and uncertainty quantification rather than a single benchmark dataset.
watch_item: A key concern is whether AI-assisted results remain physically reliable, since success depends on enforcing symmetries, conservation laws, causality, stability, and robust uncertainty quantification.
paper_title: Machine Learning Meets High-Energy Nuclear Physics: From Pattern Recognition to Physics-Integrated Discovery
